name: Lancaster
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lancaster, TX 2026
seo_description: Lancaster's 71st Christmas Parade and Wonka Land festival, the Town Square tree lighting, Cookies with Santa and 12 Days Till Christmas activities.
lede: The story of Christmas in Lancaster runs through its Historic Town Square, where the city has held a Christmas parade and festival for 70 years, with the 2026 parade billed as the 71st. Each December the tree lighting in the square breezeway, a themed parade down N. Dallas Avenue and a countdown of daily recreation center activities fill the weeks before Christmas.
sections: A parade 71 years in the making

The City of Lancaster called its 2025 Christmas Parade and Festival the 70th annual and described it as seven decades of a beloved tradition. The parade starts at Beverly D. Humphrey Stadium on E. Wintergreen Road and travels down N. Dallas Avenue to Historic Downtown Lancaster at 100 W. Main Street, where the festival continues. Each year has a theme. In 2025 it was A Polar Express Adventure, and for 2026, the 71st parade, the city is turning downtown into Wonka Land with A Willy Wonka Christmas, free toys for children, rides, games, food and vendors on the square after the parade.

Abram Bledsoe laid out Lancaster in 1852 near the older settlement of Pleasant Run and named it after his birthplace, Lancaster, Kentucky, according to the Handbook of Texas. The town was incorporated on May 22, 1887. Its square became the center of town life, and the Handbook notes that a citizens' council renovated the town square in the mid 1970s. Today the city calls it Historic Town Square, and the annual Christmas tree lighting takes place in its breezeway, a short walk from the spot where the Christmas parade ends each December.
Rails, the Interurban and trains near Lancaster

Lancaster grew up with the railroads. The Handbook of Texas records that the Dallas and Waco railroad was built through town in 1888, that the Lancaster Tap Railroad linked Lancaster to the Houston and Texas Central at Hutchins in 1890, and that the Waco Dallas Interurban connected the town to Waco in 1911. Today the nearest DART light rail is the Blue Line, whose southern end is UNT Dallas Station. From downtown Dallas, EBJ Union Station is served by DART, the Trinity Railway Express and Amtrak, and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs vintage streetcars through Uptown.
celebrates: Lancaster celebrates Christmas mostly in public spaces run by the city. The season opens with the tree lighting in the Historic Town Square breezeway, then the Christmas Parade and Festival brings floats, performers and community groups from Beverly D. Humphrey Stadium to the square, where children receive free toys. Lancaster Parks and Recreation follows with 12 Days Till Christmas, a festive activity each day from December 13 to 24, such as a scavenger hunt at Reflection Pond, carols around a campfire at Roy Crawford Park and Cookies with Santa. The city says no recreation center membership is needed to join in.
lastyear: In 2025 Lancaster marked the 70th annual Christmas Parade and Festival on Saturday, December 13, with the theme A Polar Express Adventure. The city scheduled the parade from 1 to 5 pm, starting at Beverly D. Humphrey Stadium at 200 E. Wintergreen Road and finishing at Historic Downtown Lancaster at 100 W. Main Street, where the celebration continued. The city promoted it as 70 years of Lancaster Christmas magic and said it was going bigger than ever for the milestone year.
facts: Lancaster is named for Lancaster, Kentucky, the birthplace of founder Abram Bledsoe. During the Civil War a factory in town made the Tucker Sherrod Colt Dragoon pistol for Confederate troops from Texas. The Randlett House, a two story Victorian home, was built in 1896, and the Rawlins Homestead dates to 1855. The Handbook of Texas also notes that the Commemorative Air Force Ghost Squadron was based at Lancaster Airport.
trains: Lancaster had trains early: the Dallas and Waco railroad came through in 1888, the short Lancaster Tap Railroad opened in 1890, and the Waco Dallas Interurban arrived in 1911. Today DART light rail does not reach Lancaster; the Blue Line ends to the north at UNT Dallas Station. EBJ Union Station in downtown Dallas is served by DART rail, the Trinity Railway Express and Amtrak, and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley is a vintage streetcar ride in Uptown Dallas.

kidfact: Lancaster got its name because its founder, Abram Bledsoe, was born in another town called Lancaster, in Kentucky, and he named his new Texas town after home.
faq: How long has Lancaster had a Christmas parade?

The City of Lancaster billed its 2025 Christmas Parade and Festival as the 70th annual, and the 2026 parade on December 12 is the 71st. The parade runs from Beverly D. Humphrey Stadium down N. Dallas Avenue to Historic Town Square, where a festival with rides, games, food and free toys for children follows.
What is the theme of the 2026 Lancaster Christmas parade?

A Willy Wonka Christmas. The city is turning downtown into Wonka Land for the 71st annual parade and festival, and the recreation center's Hunt for the Hat scavenger hunt follows the same theme, with Oompa Loompas hiding Willy's hat around Reflection Pond at Community Park.
Where does Lancaster light its Christmas tree?

In the breezeway of Historic Town Square at 100 W. Main Street. The 2026 ceremony is Monday, December 7, from 6 to 6:45 pm. The square was laid out with the town in the 1850s and was renovated by a citizens' council in the mid 1970s, according to the Handbook of Texas.
Is there a train near Lancaster at Christmas?

Lancaster has no passenger rail of its own today. The DART Blue Line ends at UNT Dallas Station, and downtown Dallas has EBJ Union Station with DART, the Trinity Railway Express and Amtrak. The McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley in Uptown Dallas runs vintage streetcars, a fun ride for train loving kids.
